    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:

          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: ".*\\S.*"
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: ".*\\S.*"
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: When true, allow creating this owner even if another owner has the same last name and address.

          example: false
      required:
        - firstName

        - address

## Summary

I implemented `namesakeCount` following the repo's existing `customerCode`/`householdId` pattern — a persisted owner field computed by a small pipeline function at create time and auto-mapped into the response DTO.

Changes:
1. **`CountNamesakes.java`** (new) — one cohesive function class (WMC_other = 0). Iterates existing owners before save and counts those sharing the same first + last name case-insensitively, then records it on the owner. Because it runs before `SaveOwner`, the new owner is excluded from its own count.
2. **`owners.POST.yml`** — wired the `countNamesakes` step into the create pipeline (after `assignCode`, before `save`), under the same `transaction` governance.
3. **`Owner.java`** — added a `namesakeCount` field with a `namesake_count` column plus a plain getter/setter (each CC 1). MapStruct then maps it into `OwnerDto` automatically by name — no mapper change needed.
4. **`openapi.yml`** — added the read-only `namesakeCount` (integer, int32) property to the `Owner` schema so the generated DTO exposes it.
5. **`db/hsqldb/schema.sql`** + **`db/hsqldb/data.sql`** — added the `namesake_count` column (matching the precedent that these evolving columns live only in the test DB schema) and a trailing `NULL` value to the 10 positional seed inserts so they still match the column count.

Structural impact was kept low by putting the new behaviour in its own tiny class rather than growing an existing large one, and by relying on MapStruct's by-name mapping to avoid touching the mapper.
